sources.entry: BetterPiP - Use native picture-in-picture with browsers such as Google Chrome for HTML5 videos.

summary.one_liner: BetterPiP is an archived macOS project that enables Safari-style native picture-in-picture for HTML5 videos in Firefox and Google Chrome.
summary.what_it_does: It brings the native macOS picture-in-picture framework, which Safari uses internally, to Firefox and Google Chrome. According to the README, it lets you watch HTML5 videos from sites such as YouTube and Vimeo in native PiP mode. It also states that it can put any public URL into picture-in-picture mode. The project is based on Stephen Radford's PiPHack. The README notes the author has archived the repo because Firefox and Chrome now ship their own picture-in-picture features. It is kept as a reference for learning how to use the macOS PIP.framework.
use_cases: watch YouTube videos in a floating window on macOS
use native picture-in-picture in Chrome or Firefox
learn how to use the macOS PIP.framework
float any public web video above other windows
how_to_run: Build the project yourself (the README says no prebuilt app is provided and an Apple Developer License is needed for signing)
stack: Objective-C or Swift (not named in README)
browser integration for Firefox and Google Chrome
notable: Brings Safari-style native macOS picture-in-picture to Firefox and Chrome
Works with any public URL, not only HTML5 video sites
Serves as a reference for the macOS PIP.framework
caveats: Archived: the author stopped maintaining it because Firefox and Chrome now have their own picture-in-picture
Must be built manually; the author does not have an Apple Developer License
